title: Alder-Poached Salmon with Grapefruit-Dill Sauce
description: Thin salmon portions start in alder-smoked broth and finish gently in steam with a smooth grapefruit-dill sauce.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly
Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with food probe and bottom drip pan

ingredients.name: skinless boneless salmon fillet
ingredients.note: Fully thawed, pin bones removed; divide into two portions about 3/4 inch thick.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: smooth Löwensenf Bavarian mustard
ingredients.note: Pass through a fine sieve if visibly grainy.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 250°F with alder pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Set the finishing oven
steps.text: While the liquid smokes, install the bottom drip pan in the Anova Gen 1 and preheat to 140°F, sous vide mode on, 100% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off. Set the food probe target to 139°F.

steps.title: Start the poach
steps.text: Slip {salmon} into the smoked broth, adding {topup} to just cover if necessary. Cover the pot immediately. No stall-wrap temperature applies.

steps.title: Transfer before the center is done
steps.text: Poach covered on the Traeger at 250°F, checking sideways after 3 minutes and then every 1–2 minutes. Move each piece to a clean, room-temperature shallow metal pan as soon as it reaches 125°F in the center; leave the hot poaching liquid behind.

steps.title: Finish in bagless steam
steps.text: Insert the APO probe sideways into the thicker center. Cook unbagged in the preheated APO, usually 12–35 minutes, until the probe reads 139°F.

steps.title: Make the sauce base
steps.text: While the fish finishes, measure 3/4 cup of the poaching liquid into the HexClad, adding {topup} if needed. Whisk in {juice}, {maple} and {mustard} and bring to a full boil.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the centers
steps.text: Check each thickest center with a fork: the flesh must be opaque throughout and flake apart easily. If either center is translucent or resists flaking, keep it in the 140°F full-steam oven and recheck in 3-minute intervals until both cues are met.

steps.title: Rest the fish
steps.text: Rest the fish for 2 minutes on the warm serving plates under a loose cover.

steps.title: Finish with dill
steps.text: Fold {dill} into the sauce off heat. Spoon it around the fish and over each flake as you portion it.

notes: Make ahead: Smoke the broth a day ahead and chill it promptly. Bring it back to a simmer before poaching. Option A uses grapefruit and mustard. For gentler Option B, omit both and finish with extra dill. The first-cook target is 139–140°F plus fully opaque, easily flaking flesh; the separate 165°F target below is for reheating leftovers. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The soft flakes tend to break and firm up through freezing and reheating; cook two portions fresh. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and follow the fridge reheating directions. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 293 kcal, 27.1 g protein, 5.7 g total carbohydrate, 17.2 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 96 mg sodium. The estimate uses farmed Atlantic salmon. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
